subject: chopperMotorbike
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: custom chopper motorbike.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm examining the renders to pinpoint the main design flaws—the exhaust pipes look oversized, drooping, and clunky with a tarnished steel finish, and they run awkwardly close to the engine's lower region on the left side.

I want to swap the grimy speckled steel look for a cleaner cel-shaded light steel palette, and tone down the dark panelled engine color to something more Overwatch-styled navy. I'm also reconsidering the fork design—the panelled gunmetal lower sliders read noisy, so I'm thinking of keeping panelling only on the engine and using a plain cel color for the fork legs instead.

Going through the rest of the bike part by part—front fork rake, wheels, fender, chain sweep, seat placement, headlight, mirror orientation, handlebar cables, frame tubes, and engine cylinder fins—most elements check out fine as is, aside from the rod needing to switch from the panelled gunmetal to plain gunmetal while the crankcase keeps its panelling.

I'm checking the foot peg placement, verifying ground clearance for both wheels sits at zero with the kickstand properly stowed, and considering adding an Overwatch-style glow treatment—a cyan hard-light strip along the lower frame, a glowing hologram ring, an orange fender emblem, and cyan-glowing exhaust tips.

Now I'm fine-tuning the exhaust geometry itself, adjusting the radii taper and the ring placement along the pipe so the cyan bands don't look too chunky, and considering adding a dark inner disc to close off the open pipe end instead of leaving it capless.

I'm also considering adding small Overwatch-style hard-light fin details near the seat, like angular cyan-edged tail fairings on each side, though keeping them modest so they don't overpower the design.

Then I'm adding glowing cyan underglow rods along the frame bottom and skid plate edges for extra lighting detail. I'm also planning edits to the palette definitions, switching the STEEL and GUN materials to cel-shaded versions since GUN is used on the engine fins and chain, while keeping the tank's gradient stripe paint as is.

I'm deciding the fork lowers should use orange instead of gunmetal to contrast with the steel uppers, matching the orange front fender, while leaving the navy frame pieces untouched. For the exhaust, I'm locating the unique search lines for the sweep radii and the glowing cyan ring elements to target for editing.
